After the crash, Aiden was arrested and initially charged with, driving under the influence, DUI with property damage, resisting arrest without violence, battery on a law enforcement officer, a third-degree felony, and leaving the scene of a crash causing damage over $50. over $50. She was held on a $6,500 bond, which she later posted. During a subsequent court appearance, the prosecutor dismissed the felony battery and DUI charges entirely. Aiden entered a plea of no contest to resisting an officer without violence, leaving the scene of a crash and a reduced charge of reckless driving involving alcohol. The judge adjudicated her guilty on all three counts. She was sentenced to six months of supervised probation, running concurrently across all counts in order to complete 50 hours of community service. Her probation conditions required her to complete a four-hour basic driver improvement school, a level one DUI school, and a victim awareness program. She is also subject to random urinalysis and prohibited from possessing or consuming alcohol or illegal drugs. Her total fines, court costs and fees amounted to $891.50.
